intro: Elleholm, a place in Karlshamn municipality in Blekinge, southern Sweden, has one tree on our map: Elleholmseken, a broad pedunculate oak that a reader photographed in a clearing in spring. They gave it a girth of 785 centimetres and an age of about 300 years, and their note says that red-listed lichens grow on its bark, among them old-oak lichen, and that the fruiting bodies of the beefsteak fungus show on it in some years. A path leads to the clearing.

trees.name: Elleholmseken (The Oak of Elleholm)
trees.age_estimate: about 300 years, by a reader's estimate
trees.story:
Elleholmseken stands alone in a clearing near Elleholm in Blekinge, Sweden, a broad pedunculate oak whose crown spreads in a wide dark web of branches. A reader photographed it in spring, when the first leaves were only a green haze on the twigs, and gave us a girth of 785 centimetres and an age of 300 years.

Their note is in Swedish. “På eken växer rödlistade arter som gammalekslav, grå skärelav och matt pricklav. Vissa år syns också oxtungsvampens fruktkroppar.” In English, red-listed species grow on the oak, among them old-oak lichen, a grey lichen and a dull pin lichen, and in some years the fruiting bodies of the beefsteak fungus show on it.

We found no register entry or survey for this tree, so the girth and the age are the reader's figures. A trunk of nearly eight metres round is a big one for an oak, and lichens that are on a red list tell their own story of a tree that has stood a long time in the light.

A path leads to the clearing, and a waymarker post stands beside the trunk.

question_meta: Elleholmseken is a large oak at Elleholm in Blekinge, Sweden. Where it stands and what grows on it.
question_answer: A reader photographed Elleholmseken, a pedunculate oak (Quercus robur) at Elleholm in Blekinge, and gave a girth of 785 cm and an age of about 300 years. Their note says red-listed lichens grow on the oak.
question_context: Everything this page says comes from one reader's photograph, figures and note, sent through the app. We found no register entry or published survey for the tree, so the girth of 785 centimetres and the age of about 300 years are the reader's. Their note, written in Swedish, says that red-listed species grow on the oak, among them old-oak lichen (gammalekslav), a grey lichen (grå skärelav) and a dull pin lichen (matt pricklav), and that in some years the fruiting bodies of the beefsteak fungus (oxtungssvamp) show on it. The photograph shows a single large oak with a wide, many-limbed crown in an open clearing, just coming into leaf, with a waymarker post beside its trunk. We found no published terms for access to the land, so follow any signs. If you have measured the trunk or know the tree's history, tell us on the page and it goes into this answer.
